verses.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचपरं भूयः प्रवक्ष्यामि ज्ञानानां ज्ञानमुत्तमम् । यज्ज्ञात्वा मुनयः सर्वे परां सिद्धिमितो गताः ॥
verses.tr: The Blessed Lord says: I will speak again of the highest knowledge, the best of all knowledge. Knowing this, all sages have reached the supreme perfection from here.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just described the field and the knower of the field, and now he promises a deeper truth. What is the one knowledge that frees everyone? Listen to how he introduces it.

body.text: The Blessed Lord says: I will speak again of the highest knowledge, the best of all knowledge. Knowing this, all sages have reached the supreme perfection from here. Krishna calls this the paramah jnanam, the highest knowledge. He is not offering a new subject, but the final knowledge that ends all seeking, the very same knowledge that carried all the sages to perfection. He explains that those who take refuge in this knowledge attain his likeness, never to be born again at the next creation.

verses.sa: इदं ज्ञानमुपाश्रित्य मम साधर्म्यमागताः । सर्गेऽपि नोपजायन्ते प्रलये न व्यथन्ति च ॥
verses.tr: Having taken refuge in this knowledge, they attain my likeness. They are not born at creation, and they are not troubled at dissolution.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna speaks of a knowledge that changes a person's relationship to time itself. Listen to how he describes the one who takes refuge in it.

body.text: Having taken refuge in this knowledge, they attain my likeness. They are not born at creation, and they are not troubled at dissolution. The word upashritya means taking refuge, and it shows a deliberate choice to align with the divine. Those who make this choice share Krishna's likeness and are untouched by creation and dissolution. He calls his primal nature a womb, and says he places the seed in it, so that all beings are born.

verses.sa: मम योनिर्महद्ब्रह्म तस्मिन् गर्भं दधाम्यहम् । संभवः सर्वभूतानां ततो भवति भारत ॥
verses.tr: O Bharata, my primal nature is the womb; I place the seed in it. From that, all beings are born.
verses.angle: Yoni, the womb, as the source of all beings
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna points to the source of all beings. Listen to the word that names this origin.

body.text: O Bharata, my primal nature is the womb; I place the seed in it. From that, all beings are born. Yoni means womb, and it names the source from which every being comes. Krishna places the seed in that origin, and from there all life is born. He then names himself as the seed-giving father of every living form.

verses.sa: सर्वयोनिषु कौन्तेय मूर्तयः सम्भवन्ति याः । तासां ब्रह्म महद्योनिरहं बीजप्रदः पिता ॥
verses.tr: O son of Kunti, in all forms of birth, the material nature is the womb, and I am the seed-giving father.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just called material nature the womb. Now he tells Arjuna that he is the father who places the seed.

body.text: O son of Kunti, in all forms of birth, the material nature is the womb, and I am the seed-giving father. Listen to the pairing of father and mother, seed-giving father and womb. Krishna says that whatever body is born, he is the one who plants the seed. Krishna then explains how the three qualities of nature bind the inner self to the body.

verses.sa: सत्त्वं रजस्तम इति गुणाः प्रकृतिसंभवाः । निबध्नन्ति महाबाहो देहे देहिनमव्ययम् ॥
verses.tr: Arjuna, the three qualities of nature, sattva, rajas, and tamas, bind the imperishable inner being to the body.
verses.angle: Nibadhnanti: the binding power of the gunas
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: The previous verse spoke of the seed and the womb. Now Krishna names the forces born from that union.

body.text: Arjuna, the three qualities of nature, sattva, rajas, and tamas, bind the imperishable inner being to the body. The word nibadhnanti means bind. The three qualities do not merely color life, they tie the deathless self to the body, so even sattva is a chain. Krishna now turns to sattva alone, showing that even purity and light keep the self tied to the body.

verses.sa: तत्र सत्त्वं निर्मलत्वात्प्रकाशकमनामयम् । सुखसङ्गेन बध्नाति ज्ञानसङ्गेन चानघ ॥
verses.tr: Among those qualities, sattva, because it is pure and luminous and free from affliction, binds the embodied being through attachment to happiness and to knowledge, O sinless one.
verses.angle: sattva binds through happiness and knowledge
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has named sattva as pure and bright. But why does he warn that this quality still binds? Listen to the two chains he names.

body.text: Among those qualities, sattva, because it is pure and luminous and free from affliction, binds the embodied being through attachment to happiness and to knowledge, O sinless one. Even sattva, which is free from affliction, binds the embodied being through attachment to happiness and to knowledge, O sinless one. Krishna now turns to rajas, born of craving, and names the chain of action.

verses.sa: रजो रागात्मकं विद्धि तृष्णासङ्गसमुद्भवम् । तन्निबध्नाति कौन्तेय कर्मसङ्गेन देहिनम् ॥
verses.tr: Know rajas as passion-born, born of craving and attachment. It binds the embodied being through attachment to action, O son of Kunti.
verses.angle: Rajas binds the embodied being through attachment to action
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna continues his lesson on the three forces. He now names the restless force that keeps a person tied to action.

body.text: Know rajas as passion-born, born of craving and attachment. It binds the embodied being through attachment to action, O son of Kunti. Krishna names rajas as born from craving and attachment, and he says that force binds the embodied being through attachment to action. Krishna goes on to name the third force, tamas, born of ignorance and sleep.

verses.sa: तमस्त्वज्ञानजं विद्धि मोहनं सर्वदेहिनाम् । प्रमादालस्यनिद्राभिस्तन्निबध्नाति भारत ॥
verses.tr: Arjuna, know tamas to be born of ignorance and deluding all embodied beings. It binds them through heedlessness, laziness, and sleep.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna points to the final quality, tamas, and asks you to hear the one word that describes its grip on every living being.

body.text: Arjuna, know tamas to be born of ignorance and deluding all embodied beings. It binds them through heedlessness, laziness, and sleep. Listen to mohanam, deluding. It is not a physical weapon but a veil that clouds the mind of every embodied being, making the truth invisible to them. Krishna now names the three things that tamas uses to keep beings bound in darkness.

verses.sa: सत्त्वं सुखे सञ्जयति रजः कर्मणि भारत । ज्ञानमावृत्य तु तमः प्रमादे सञ्जयत्युत ॥
verses.tr: Sattva binds through pleasure, rajas through action, and tamas, covering knowledge, binds through negligence.
verses.angle: Sanajayati: the word that binds all three gunas
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna is finishing his list of the three forces that shape the world. Listen to the one word that unites them.

body.text: Sattva binds through pleasure, rajas through action, and tamas, covering knowledge, binds through negligence. The Sanskrit word Sanajayati means binds, and it binds all three: Sattva through pleasure, Rajas through action, and Tamas through negligence. Krishna then explains how the three forces take turns rising when the other two are subdued.

verses.sa: रजस्तमश्चाभिभूय सत्त्वं भवति भारत । रजः सत्त्वं तमश्चैव तमः सत्त्वं रजस्तथा ॥
verses.tr: Arjuna, when rajas and tamas are subdued, sattva rises. When sattva and tamas are subdued, rajas rises. When sattva and rajas are subdued, tamas rises.
verses.angle: Overpowering: one quality rises by crushing the others
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Last we saw how each guna binds. Now listen to how they battle one another to take the lead.

body.text: Arjuna, when rajas and tamas are subdued, sattva rises. When sattva and tamas are subdued, rajas rises. When sattva and rajas are subdued, tamas rises. The gunas compete: one rises by pressing down the other two, so inner states keep changing. Krishna now shows how sattva makes itself known when it grows strong in the body.

verses.sa: सर्वद्वारेषु देहेऽस्मिन्प्रकाश उपजायते । ज्ञानं यदा तदा विद्याद्विवृद्धं सत्त्वमित्युत ॥
verses.tr: When light, clarity, and understanding arise in all the gates of this body, know that sattva has grown strong.
verses.angle: Light in the gates signals sattva
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has been describing the three qualities that bind us. Now he gives a clear sign. Listen for the moment when light arises inside the body's gates.

body.text: When light, clarity, and understanding arise in all the gates of this body, know that sattva has grown strong. Krishna does not point to an outside sign. He points to the body itself, to the gates, the senses and the mind, saying that when light arises inside them, you can know sattva is growing. Krishna then turns to the opposite sign, showing how rajas, activity, and desire arise when that same inner light is missing.

verses.sa: लोभः प्रवृत्तिरारम्भः कर्मणामशमः स्पृहा । रजस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे भरतर्षभ ॥
verses.tr: O best of the Bharatas, when rajas grows, greed, activity, the beginning of actions, restlessness, and desire arise.
verses.angle: Ashamah, restlessness, is the sign of rajas
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna turns from the calm of sattva to the restless force of rajas. Listen for the five signs of this growing energy.

body.text: O best of the Bharatas, when rajas grows, greed, activity, the beginning of actions, restlessness, and desire arise. Krishna lists the marks of rising rajas: greed, busy activity, fresh undertakings, restlessness and desire. Krishna then turns to tamas, the opposite darkness that brings delusion and inertia.

verses.sa: अप्रकाशोऽप्रवृत्तिश्च प्रमादो मोह एव च । तमस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे कुरुनन्दन ॥
verses.tr: O descendant of Kuru, when tamas grows strong, darkness, inertia, negligence, and delusion arise.
verses.angle: tamas increases and four things are born
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna asks you to listen for the exact chain of events that follows when tamas grows.

body.text: O descendant of Kuru, when tamas grows strong, darkness, inertia, negligence, and delusion arise. Krishna lists four things born from tamas: darkness, inertia, negligence, and delusion. They arrive in sequence as the quality of tamas increases and takes over. Sanjaya now describes what happens when sattva predominates at the time of death.

verses.sa: यदा सत्त्वे प्रवृद्धे तु प्रलयं याति देहभृत् । तदोत्तमविदां लोकानमलान्प्रतिपद्यते ॥
verses.tr: When sattva is predominant at death, the embodied being reaches the pure worlds of the wise.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna explains the path that opens when clarity, sattva, is strongest at the moment of death. Listen for how he names the destination.

body.text: When sattva is predominant at death, the embodied being reaches the pure worlds of the wise. Listen for the word amalan, pure or stainless. The embodied one reaches the pure worlds where the wise dwell. Krishna then turns to rajas, the force of action, and shows how it shapes the next birth.

verses.sa: रजसि प्रलयं गत्वा कर्मसङ्गिषु जायते । तथा प्रलीनस्तमसि मूढयोनिषु जायते ॥
verses.tr: A being who dies in rajas is born among those attached to action. A being who dies in tamas is born among deluded forms.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna finishes the picture of the gunas by looking at the two lower paths. Listen to how the state of mind at death shapes the next birth.

body.text: A being who dies in rajas is born among those attached to action. A being who dies in tamas is born among deluded forms. One word reveals the fate of restless desire, rajas. A being who dies in rajas is born among those attached to action, caught again in the very cycle of work that binds them. Krishna now explains that the result of rajasic action is suffering, while the result of tamasic action is ignorance and delusion.
